title: The autocomplete bug, step by step
intro: The same rejected selection, with the old action and with the fixed one. Watch where each one decides that it succeeded.

flows.label: Before the fix
flows.summary: The action checks the text it typed, and reports a success that never happened.

steps.title: The action types the value
steps.text: To find the option, the action types its label into the input. This part is the same before and after the fix.

steps.title: The input now says USD
steps.text: The input contains the typed text. In an autocomplete, that text is only a filter. It is not the field's value.

steps.title: The selection doesn't commit
steps.text: The option is clicked, but nothing is saved: in production the list hadn't finished loading; in Pagewright's test the component rejects the change. Either way, MUI holds no value.

steps.title: The check reads the typed text
steps.text: The old action asserted toHaveValue(value) right away. The input still holds the text the action typed two lines earlier, so the assertion passes, and the action reports success.

steps.title: MUI never saved anything
steps.text: The real state, the selected value, was never part of the check. Nothing in the test knows it is empty.

steps.title: The test fails far from the cause
steps.text: When the field loses focus, MUI clears the unselected text. The form is submitted with an empty field, and the test fails three steps later with a validation error that points nowhere near the autocomplete.

flows.label: After the fix
flows.summary: The action checks what MUI saved, so a rejected selection fails at the autocomplete itself.

steps.title: The action types the value
steps.text: Same as before: type the label to filter the list.

steps.title: The option is clicked
steps.text: The option is clicked by its accessible name. With the rejecting component, the click happens but nothing is saved, exactly as before.
steps.code: await input.page().getByRole('option', { name: option, exact: true }).click();

steps.title: The action leaves the field
steps.text: The new step: blur. In MUI's default mode, text that wasn't selected is cleared when the field loses focus.

steps.title: Only a saved value survives
steps.text: After blur, the input shows the selected value's label, or nothing. The typed text can no longer pretend to be a selection.

steps.title: The check now means something
steps.text: The same toHaveValue, after blur, can only pass if MUI really saved the option. With a rejected selection the input is empty, and the action fails right here, at the autocomplete, with a clear message.
